answer.rationale: Competitor price cut creates acute pressure on SMB retention. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is ruled out due to documented 30-day retention harm despite acquisition lift. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) addresses wrong segment. Referral incentives (memory_57) work for established customers but don't address immediate churn risk. Instead, deploy in-product activation messaging (memory_91: +11% week-one engagement, +6% activation, +1% retention) paired with shortened onboarding (memory_86: +13% completion, -2.1 days TTv, +3% retention) across at-risk SMB accounts. This combination targets engagement velocity and time-to-value—reducing perceived friction that price-cut messaging exploits—without eroding retention or unit economics. The strategy reinforces product stickiness rather than competing on price. Standard experiment scope allows controlled rollout to churn-risk cohorts while preserving ability to escalate if needed. Risk is low: both interventions are confirmed, additive, and aligned with long-term qualified revenue objective.
